chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Hamzah ibn Ya'la from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the crescent of Rajab is confirmed, count fifty-nine days and fast the sixtieth day." He means by his saying (peace be upon him), 'fast the sixtieth day,' on the assumption that it is from Sha'ban, as a precaution. And that which reveals what we mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.صَحَّ هِلَالُ رَجَبٍ: The crescent of Rajab is confirmed/verified

ai.seo_question: How to determine the first day of Ramadan when the crescent sighting is uncertain?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the 'Day of Doubt' (Yawm al-Shakk) protocol, where fasting on the 30th of Sha'ban serves as a precautionary fulfillment of the Ramadan obligation if the month is determined to be twenty-nine days. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of combining certainty with precaution in lunar calendar calculations, ensuring the integrity of the month's worship despite astronomical uncertainties.
